review.proposal: Freeze the seven passing configurations and do not learn from FINAL. Quarantine IPUSDT and every symbol with a nonzero data-failure indicator; repair provenance/alignment/completeness first and rerun unchanged. For clean near-threshold symbols, run DEV-only, one-variable-at-a-time tests grouped narrowly by symbol: (1) DOT/ONDO/PNUT/SHIB/TIA/XPLUS and JP225/US500/AUDCAD: inspect DEV-versus-VALIDATION regime composition and geometry boundaries; (2) SOL: test a minimal entry-confirmation or stop/target-geometry adjustment aimed at split stability; (3) FIL/LIT/NEAR and NAS100: test only adjacent geometry values. Each candidate must retain RR exactly 1 or 2 and 1-3 executions per eligible day, with no symbol pooling, sample deletion, synthetic data, or cross-split leakage. Revalidate independently and accept only if every exact-data check passes, both DEV and VALIDATION achieve WR>=80% and positive expectancy, and execution-frequency constraints hold. Do not refine the materially weak or negative-expectancy symbols until trade-level regime/geometry evidence is available.

review.proposal: Implement strict data partitioning protocols ensuring no leakage between dev and validation sets. For each failing symbol, propose a refined regime-specific parameter adjustment (e.g., reduce entry threshold by 10%) while maintaining RR=1.0 and WR >= 80%. Conduct targeted regression testing on top 5 worst-performing symbols before re-evaluation.
